_doc: LOCK IS INHERITED, NOT MATERIALIZED — the cross-language family for
transcripts/LAYER_STRUCTURE.md §13 (RULED by JYH 2026-07-28): a locked
layer locks everything inside it, at every depth, and those elements
cannot be individually unlocked.
WHY THIS FAMILY COULD NOT EXIST BEFORE TODAY. Every case here is seeded
from a setup_svg, and until LOCKSVG (§13.1) the SVG codec dropped
`common.locked` in both active ports — so no shared fixture anywhere
could START from a locked document. That is why the corpus stayed green
over an enforcement gap this wide. `jas:locked="true"` in locked_
inheritance.svg is what makes these vectors expressible at all.
THE DOCUMENT (SVG px -> document pt is x3/4, so x=32 lands at 24):
[0]     Layer 'Locked Layer'   jas:locked  — the INHERITANCE source
[0,0]      rect                 own flag FALSE, locked by ancestry
[0,1]      group 'Inner Group'  own flag FALSE, locked by ancestry
[0,1,0]      rect               own flag FALSE, locked at DEPTH 2
[1]     Layer 'Open Layer'     unlocked
[1,0]      rect      jas:locked — own lock inside an UNLOCKED layer
[1,1]      group 'Locked Group' jas:locked
[1,1,0]      rect               own flag FALSE, child of a locked GROUP
[1,2]      rect                 free — the control
[1,3]      group 'Mixed Group'  unlocked
[1,3,0]      rect      jas:locked — a locked leaf inside an open group
[1,3,1]      rect                 free
WHAT EACH VERB DRIVES. `select_element` is the path-addressed click seam
(jas_dioxus Controller::select_element, JasSwift Controller.selectElement)
— the two adjacent lines the scope named as the smoking gun, where the
element's OWN `locked` was read one line above an INHERITED
effective_visibility. `select_rect` is the marquee (select_flat /
selectFlat). Both op verbs route through the SAME Controller mutator the
production UI calls, never a test-only shortcut.
SELECTION-ONLY: neither verb is undoable, so these cases journal nothing
and the checkpoint_equivalence gate replays an empty prefix.
PINNED BUT NOT RULED — `click_a_free_member_of_a_mixed_group_selects_the
_whole_group` keeps the shipped group-click rule (clicking any member
selects the group AND every child) even though one of those children is
locked. Whether a group selection may contain a locked member is a
question §13 does not answer; the golden makes the day of that ruling a
visible byte change rather than a silent drift.
name: lock_inheritance_setup_is_a_locked_layer_and_an_open_one

_doc: The headline vector. [0,0] carries NO lock flag of its own; it is locked because its LAYER is. Before the ruling both ports selected it.
name: click_a_child_of_a_locked_layer_is_refused

_doc: Inheritance is not one level deep. [0,1,0] is a grandchild of the locked layer, and its own flag and its group's are both false. Before the ruling this selected the group AND the leaf.
name: click_a_grandchild_of_a_locked_layer_is_refused

_doc: The unlocked GROUP inside the locked layer is itself unselectable. Its own flag is false; only its ancestor's is set.
name: click_an_unlocked_group_inside_a_locked_layer_is_refused

_doc: A child of a locked GROUP, at depth, inside an UNLOCKED layer — so the refusal cannot be explained by the layer. Before the ruling this selected [1,1] and [1,1,0].
name: click_a_child_of_a_locked_group_is_refused

_doc: A leaf with its OWN lock, inside an unlocked layer. This was already refused before the ruling and must STAY refused — the regression guard that keeps the new inherited read from replacing the own-flag read instead of subsuming it.
name: click_an_element_locked_inside_an_unlocked_layer_is_refused

_doc: A leaf with its OWN lock inside an UNLOCKED group. Before the ruling clicking it selected the group and both its children.
name: click_a_locked_leaf_inside_an_open_group_is_refused

_doc: The locked LAYER itself, and then the locked GROUP itself. Both were already refused by the own-flag read; both must stay refused.
name: click_the_locked_layer_itself_is_refused

_doc: The control: a free leaf in an unlocked layer still selects. Without this the whole family would be satisfied by a select_element that refused EVERYTHING.
name: click_a_free_element_still_selects

_doc: PINNED, NOT RULED (see the family _doc). Clicking the free member of Mixed Group selects the group and EVERY child, including the locked [1,3,0]. §13 rules on what may be SELECTED by pointing at it, not on what a container selection sweeps up.
name: click_a_free_member_of_a_mixed_group_selects_the_whole_group

_doc: MARQUEE over the whole document. Everything under the locked layer, the locked leaf, the locked group and the locked leaf inside the open group are all excluded; the free leaf and the open group with its free child survive.
name: marquee_over_the_whole_document_takes_only_the_unlocked

_doc: MARQUEE confined to the locked layer's own artwork. Nothing is taken — the locked layer's whole subtree is out of reach.
name: marquee_over_a_locked_layer_takes_nothing

_doc: MARQUEE confined to the child of the locked GROUP, in the UNLOCKED layer. Nothing is taken.
name: marquee_over_a_locked_groups_child_takes_nothing

_doc: MARQUEE confined to the LOCKED leaf inside the OPEN group. A locked element must not be able to drag its unlocked siblings into a selection: before the ruling this rubber-band took the group and BOTH its children even though the only thing the rectangle touched was locked.
name: marquee_over_only_a_locked_member_of_an_open_group_takes_nothing
